calibrations.method_notes: Harmonized from all 74 entries in popularity_raw.json; no web lookups were made. ENGAGED = cumulative people who actually enrolled in, were treated with, bought, or meaningfully used the program at least once. Book PURCHASERS count; readers of borrowed copies do not. Registered or active app users count, but not raw downloads. AUDIENCE = cumulative unique people exposed: followers, unique viewers (YouTube views divided by about 10-30 to get unique viewers), podcast listeners, site visitors and press, and it is always >= engaged. Calibration: (1) hard numbers were taken at face value. Examples: ENO Breathe 4,829 completers, Nerva's 195k real-world dataset, NeuroStar >250k patients, Tapping Solution 868k unique users, Dispenza's 22k retreat roster, Coursera 9.8k, VA CBT-CP >=14k. (2) Unaudited company 'helped/served' claims were discounted 0.2-0.5 log10. Examples: Gupta 40k to 10^4.4, Lightning Process 75k to 10^4.6, Curable 1M+ to 10^5.6, CMBM Gaza/Haiti, Breathworks 100k. (3) Researcher reach values that were really audience were moved to audience_log10, with engaged set much lower: YouTube-led programs such as Raelan Agle, Pain Free You, CFS Health and Irene Lyon, plus Compassionate Inquiry, which uses Mate's film/book audience, and neurosymptoms.org, which uses site visits. (4) Umbrella practices count only health, clinical or self-care use relevant to chronic conditions, globally. Yoga therapy covers therapeutic or condition-specific yoga only, with general yoga (>10^8) excluded. Tai chi/qigong covers health-motivated and structured health programs only, with recreational/martial practice in China excluded. EMDR, IFS, SE, polyvagal, TMS and neurofeedback count clinical or self-care use for any chronic mental or physical condition, not pain only; pain-specific subsets are 1.5-2 log units smaller (for example, EMDR for pain is about 10^4.5). CBT and ACT count pain-specific delivery only. Interdisciplinary pain rehab counts the generic global model, of which Mayo alone is about 10^4.4. Rank check: meditation apps (7.9) > yoga therapy / tai chi (7.0-7.1) > EMDR / Relaxation Response / EFT / Wim Hof / MBSR / IFS / Dispenza / Sarno (6.1-6.6) > MBCT / PNE / CBT-CP / interdisciplinary rehab (6.0-6.2) > Curable / nVNS / Nerva / PRT (5.2-5.7) > DNRS / Gupta / LP (4.4-4.6) > small brain-retraining businesses (3.2-4.0) > PSRT (2.0). Trajectories are the researcher relative-activity curves read as relative new engaged users per year, mostly unchanged. Changes: pre-1960 total entries were added at year 1959 for Alexander (40) and Feldenkrais (6), and the CBT/GET 2011 PACE media spike was smoothed. Some curves start before the founding year, where predecessors existed (for example, the Relaxation Response from 1970). Confidence is low for most entries because the numbers are Fermi estimates. It is high only where a hard count exists (ENO Breathe, Nerva, PSRT). calibrations.method_notes:
HARMONIZED SCALES. engaged_log10 = cumulative people who enrolled in, were treated with, or meaningfully used the program at least once (book PURCHASERS count; free-content viewers do not). audience_log10 = cumulative unique people exposed (viewers, readers, listeners, site visitors), always >= engaged. Researcher reach_log10 values mixed these two definitions, so each program was re-derived.

CONVERSION RATIOS (applied explicitly; see each basis):
(1) YouTube: unique viewers = total views / 10 (/12 for long-running channels; /25 for daily-upload channels such as Pain Free You). Subscribers are about 5-10% of uniques. Creator-led paid programs convert ~1-3% of unique viewers to engaged users. A single YouTuber's views are counted as audience only.
(2) Apps: unique users = downloads x ~0.5-0.6 after repeat-install and cross-app overlap. Meaningful use (≥1 session) = ~50-65% of registered users; company 'users' or signup claims are discounted ~0.25-0.65. Rating counts are a cross-check, at roughly 1 rating per 10-15 active users (calibrated on Nerva: 32.5k iOS ratings, 3x10^5 users).
(3) Trustpilot: ~30 customers per review (calibrated on Lin Health: 613 reviews, ~2x10^4 patients).
(4) Podcasts: regular listeners = cumulative downloads / ~150.
(5) Websites: uniques = visits / ~8; ~15% use the site as structured self-help.
(6) Clinician-delivered methods: trained clinicians actually practising x clients per career (10-50 depending on intensity).
(7) Books: copies sold x ~0.8 = unique purchasers.
(8) Vendor 'reached/helped' claims are discounted 20-50% unless corroborated.

UMBRELLA PRACTICES. Yoga therapy, tai chi/qigong, EMDR, CBT for pain, neurofeedback, PNE/Explain Pain, interdisciplinary pain rehab and rTMS count only health, clinical or self-care use relevant to chronic conditions, globally. General fitness yoga (>10^8) and general Chinese park tai chi are excluded. EMDR counts all clinical (trauma/PTSD) use; pain-specific EMDR is ~10^4.5. Meditation apps, Wim Hof, nVNS consumer devices and Muse are counted as self-care use, with no pain-only restriction (noted in basis).

WEB LOOKUPS (6): Joe Dispenza YouTube ~1.74M subs (socialcounts/sponsorradar/creatordb, mid-2026); Wim Hof iOS app ~1.7M installs, ~110k MAU (AppGoblin, May 2026) plus developer claim of >1M downloads per store; Tapping Solution Android 1M+ installs, 22k US iOS ratings. Searches for subreddit sizes (r/TMSTherapy, DNRS) returned no usable counts, so subreddit and Google Trends signals were not quantified. Ranks rest on YouTube, app, Trustpilot, forum and book-sales signals instead.

SANITY ORDER CHECK: meditation apps (7.9) >> yoga therapy (7.2) > tai chi (6.9) > Wim Hof (6.6) > MBSR (6.3) ~ IFS > Sarno (6.1) > Curable (5.4) > PRT (5.2) > DNRS = Gupta (4.7) > YouTube-led programs such as Raelan Agle and CFS Health (3.9 engaged, but 5.6-6.0 audience) > re-origin (3.2) > PSRT (2.0).

TRAJECTORIES. These are researcher relative-activity points re-used as relative new engaged users per year (any scale), checked against indicators: launch years, app-store dates, the 2020-22 pandemic spike for apps and online programs, the 2021 PRT/JAMA spike, the 2017 Sarno documentary and the 2021 NICE GET reversal. Pre-1960 activity is collapsed into one 1959 entry for Alexander Technique (15) and Feldenkrais (5). For umbrella practices (yoga, tai chi), points before the named program's founding are kept because the umbrella count includes them.

Main uncertainties: book-sales figures are mostly unaudited; umbrella restriction shares are judgment calls (±0.4 log); vendor claims for small brain-retraining programs are ±0.3 log.

calibrations.method_notes:
engaged_log10 = cumulative people who enrolled in, were treated by or meaningfully used the program. That covers course or app users with at least one real session, therapy/class clients, device buyers, and book purchasers for book-based methods. audience_log10 = people exposed: YouTube and podcast viewers (views converted to unique people at roughly 10-25 views per person), site visitors, media and social reach. audience is never below engaged.

How the estimates were made: they are anchored first on institutional reach, i.e. certified practitioners x plausible caseload, clinics and hospitals, guideline adoption (NICE, VA, CDC), insurance or payer coverage, and national rollouts (NHS PMPs, VA CBT-CP, German multimodal pain therapy, Danish regional units). Vendor claims come next and are discounted about 0.1-0.3 log when unaudited. A single influencer's view count is never counted as engagement, so Raelan Agle, Dan Buglio, CFS Health, Irene Lyon and Optimum Health have wide engaged-audience gaps.

Umbrella practices (yoga therapy, tai chi/qigong, EMDR, CBT for pain, neurofeedback/biofeedback, TMS, interdisciplinary rehab, PNE, IFS, SE, polyvagal) count only use for health, clinical or self-care purposes relevant to chronic conditions, globally. Recreational fitness yoga, martial tai chi and general psychotherapy uses are excluded. EMDR and TMS include PTSD and depression treatment, since these are chronic conditions; pain-specific EMDR alone would be ~10^4.5.

Resulting rank order: meditation apps (8.0) > tai chi/qigong (7.4) ≈ yoga therapy (7.2) > EMDR, PNE, relaxation response, MBSR, CBT for pain, interdisciplinary rehab (6.3-6.6) > Sarno, IFS, Dispenza, EFT, Wim Hof (6.1-6.3) > ... > DNRS/Gupta (~4.6) > small limbic-retraining courses (3.4-3.9) > PSRT (2.0).

Trajectories are the researcher's relative-activity anchor points, kept mostly as given, rescaled as relative new engaged users per year. Interpolate linearly between the anchor years; the scale is arbitrary within each program. The only additions are pre-1960 total entries, stored as year 1959 (Alexander technique 60, Feldenkrais 5), and 1960 start points for tai chi and yoga therapy.

Web lookups were limited to 3: Nerivio (~35k US users by 2022), tai chi NHIS prevalence (1.2-1.7% of US adults, 2007-2017) and German OPS 8-918 volumes (no national total found). Everything else draws on the researcher indicators plus background knowledge. Most confidences are low; plausible error is ±0.5 log for the mid-tier and ±0.3 for well-documented items such as ENO Breathe, PSRT, Nerva and the meditation apps.
